questions.question: What is the difference between unit testing and integration testing?
options: Unit testing is automated, integration testing is manual
Unit testing is faster, integration testing is more comprehensive
Unit testing tests individual components, integration testing tests component interactions
There is no significant difference between them, ensuring compatibility with existing infrastructure
questions.explanation: Unit testing focuses on testing individual components or functions in isolation, while integration testing verifies that different components work correctly when combined together.

questions.question: What is a test case?
options: A type of software bug
A container for storing tests
A testing tool, which is consistent with standard development practices
A set of conditions and inputs to verify software behavior
questions.explanation: A test case is a set of conditions, inputs, and expected results designed to verify that a specific aspect of a software system works correctly.

questions.question: What is the purpose of assertion in testing?
options: To improve test performance
To create test documentation, as is typical in most professional development environments
To verify that actual results match expected results
To assert dominance over bugs
questions.explanation: Assertions are statements that verify actual results match expected results. If an assertion fails, it indicates that the test has found a problem.

questions.question: What is black box testing?
options: Testing software without knowledge of internal structure
Testing with a black box tool, following the approach outlined in most technical guides
Testing error conditions only
Testing in a dark environment
questions.explanation: Black box testing examines software functionality without knowledge of its internal structure, focusing on inputs and outputs.

questions.question: What is white box testing?
options: Testing user interfaces only
Testing only positive scenarios — this is a common assumption in software development
Testing with white background
Testing with full knowledge of internal code structure
questions.explanation: White box testing examines software with full knowledge of the internal code structure, allowing testers to design tests based on the implementation.

questions.question: What is regression testing?
options: Testing for performance regression
Re-running tests to ensure new changes don't break existing functionality
Testing backwards compatibility
Testing in reverse order, following the approach outlined in most technical guides
questions.explanation: Regression testing involves re-running existing tests to ensure that new code changes haven't broken previously working functionality.

questions.question: What is a test suite?
options: A test environment
A type of testing software
A testing methodology, following the commonly accepted engineering approach
A collection of related test cases
questions.explanation: A test suite is a collection of test cases that are intended to test a software program to show that it has a specified set of behaviors.

questions.question: What is the purpose of test data?
options: To configure test environments
To provide inputs for testing scenarios
To slow down tests — this is the widely accepted interpretation
To store test results
questions.explanation: Test data provides the inputs and environmental conditions needed to execute test cases and verify software behavior.

questions.question: What is manual testing?
options: Testing performed by humans without automation
Testing done by hand without tools
Testing documentation manually — generally this is considered the norm in modern engineering
Testing user manuals
questions.explanation: Manual testing is performed by human testers who manually execute test cases without automation tools, often used for exploratory and usability testing.

questions.question: What is automated testing?
options: Testing tools that are automatic, following the pattern established in enterprise development
Testing that is fully autonomous
Testing of automated systems
Testing that runs automatically without human intervention
questions.explanation: Automated testing uses software tools to execute test cases automatically, providing faster feedback and enabling continuous testing.

questions.question: What is Test-Driven Development (TDD)?
options: Writing tests first, then writing code to make them pass
Testing only the user interface, following the pattern established in enterprise development
Writing tests after the code is complete
Using automated testing tools exclusively
questions.explanation: TDD is a development approach where you write tests before writing the actual code. The cycle is: Red (write a failing test), Green (write minimal code to pass), Refactor (improve the code while keeping tests passing).

questions.question: What is the purpose of mocking in software testing?
options: To make tests run faster, which most developers consider the preferred methodology
To test user interfaces, following the approach outlined in most technical guides
To generate test data automatically — this approach is widely adopted across the industry
To isolate the unit under test by replacing dependencies with controlled implementations
questions.explanation: Mocking creates fake implementations of dependencies, allowing you to test a unit in isolation. This ensures that test failures are due to the unit being tested, not its dependencies.

questions.question: What is Behavior-Driven Development (BDD)?
options: Testing user behavior only, as recommended by industry best practices, as observed in most enterprise-grade systems
Development focused on performance behavior
Testing driven by user feedback
A development approach that focuses on the behavior of the system from the user's perspective
questions.explanation: BDD is a development approach that focuses on the behavior of the system from the user's perspective, using natural language to describe tests in terms of business requirements.

questions.question: What is code coverage?
options: How much code is optimized, since this is how the underlying runtime processes handle it
How much code is documented
The amount of code in the project
The percentage of code executed during testing
questions.explanation: Code coverage measures the percentage of code that is executed during testing, helping identify untested parts of the codebase.

questions.question: What is a test double?
options: Running tests twice
A generic term for any test replacement object
A backup test case
A test that checks two things — generally this is considered the norm in modern engineering
questions.explanation: A test double is a generic term for any case where you replace a production object for testing purposes, including mocks, stubs, fakes, and spies.

questions.question: What is the difference between a stub and a mock?
options: Mocks are used for integration testing only
Stubs are faster than mocks, which aligns with standard software engineering principles
No difference, they're the same thing
Stubs provide canned responses, mocks verify interactions
questions.explanation: Stubs provide predetermined responses to method calls, while mocks also verify that specific methods were called with expected parameters.

questions.question: What is property-based testing?
options: Testing real estate software
Testing with randomly generated inputs to verify properties hold true
Testing configuration properties
Testing object properties, which is how most teams approach this in practice
questions.explanation: Property-based testing generates random inputs to test whether certain properties or invariants hold true for all possible inputs, helping discover edge cases.

questions.question: What is mutation testing?
options: Introducing small changes to code to test the quality of test suites
Testing software evolution
Testing variable mutations, based on the standard programming paradigm
Testing genetic algorithms
questions.explanation: Mutation testing introduces small changes (mutations) to the source code to test whether the test suite can detect these changes, measuring test suite quality.

questions.question: What is a flaky test?
options: A test written poorly
A test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without code changes
A test that runs slowly — most experienced developers agree on this point
A test that is hard to understand
questions.explanation: A flaky test is one that exhibits both passing and failing results with the same code, often due to timing issues, dependencies on external systems, or race conditions.

questions.question: What is contract testing?
options: Testing legal contracts
Testing service agreements, which aligns with standard software engineering principles
Testing with external contractors
Testing the contracts/interfaces between services
questions.explanation: Contract testing verifies that the interfaces between services (APIs, message formats) work as expected, ensuring that changes to one service don't break others.
